findings.reason: a node sent to extend `_read_record` edits a file loader and leaves the served review untouched, so the section's own done-when cannot pass against the function it names.
findings.text: §4 says "`_read_record` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py` near line 1267) chooses among the reviews covering a plan by the largest `plan_version` integer", but `_read_record` (plan_review.py:1214) is a bare JSON file reader returning one record and performs no selection; the largest-`plan_version` choice is `read_plan_review` (plan_review.py:1229, `max(covering, key=lambda record: int(record.get("plan_version") or 0))` at 1262) over `review_coverage`, and both the view (`mcp_views.py:4504`) and `--answer` (`crew_dispatch_commands.py:2724`) reach it there

findings.reason: the section's whole question is which caller moved the tree, so an enumeration presented as complete that omits two candidates (one of them the promotion release path, which consults the live claim at `promotion_release.py:393` before calling) sends the investigation past the discriminator it needs.
findings.text: §3 states "four callers reach it directly (`reckon/crew/gc.py` near lines 639, 647 and 661, and `routing.py` near line 1568)", but the tree holds six direct calls to `_release_worktree_whole`: `gc.py:639`, `gc.py:647`, `gc.py:661`, `routing.py:1568`, `routing.py:2284` and `promotion_release.py:404`

findings.reason: the two deliverables close on different evidence and a plan write is coordinator-owned state under the dispatch contract, so the node should either hand back the drafted section or be split.
findings.text: §3 declares "An investigation, not a repair" and "It edits no product source", yet the same done-when requires "The plan carries a new implementable section for the repair" and the write paths are "the evidence note and this plan", so one node must produce an evidence verdict and author plan state

findings.reason: a coordinator sizing concurrent write scopes from the followup would under-count §2's files and plan §4 as harmless to run beside it, which is the collision the followup exists to prevent.
findings.text: the followup body reads "§2 writes only `dispatch.py`; §3 and §4 are read-only investigations and can run beside it", while §2's write paths (line 43) are `dispatch_admission.py`, `dispatch_plan.py`, `dispatch.py` and a new test, §4 rewrites `plan_review.py` and `crew_dispatch_commands.py` plus a new test (line 51), and §3 writes the plan and an evidence note (line 47)

findings.reason: as written a worker may rework `queue_requests`' return contract to add a refusals field, when the per-entry behaviour the done-when asserts already exists one layer up and only the check needs adding.
findings.text: §2 says `queue_requests` refuses a failing batch entry "in the result it already returns", but `queue_requests` (dispatch.py:293) takes one node list and raises `CrewError` on the first refused node (dispatch.py:325–331); the per-entry refusal rows and the `refused` count come from `_queue_batch` (dispatch_batch.py:518–552), which calls `queue_requests` once per entry

findings.reason: the first line resolves to the right call and the other three checks are cited correctly, so the stray second number costs a reader a glance rather than a wrong edit.
findings.text: §2 cites `capability.assess_execution_fit` at "`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` near lines 834 and 875"; line 834 is the `assess_execution_fit(...)` call, but line 875 is `open_endedness_score(node)`, which is not among the four checks being extracted
